result:
`guren check` reports 0 failures — the 4 warnings are pre-existing missing-test-file notices for other controllers, untouched by this change.

The excerpt was never lost from the database; it was being dropped during serialization. `PostResource.toArray()` in `app/Http/Resources/PostResource.ts` still declared `excerpt: string` on its `PostResourceData` interface, but the returned object omitted the field — so every page that reads `post.excerpt` (`posts/Index.tsx`, `posts/Show.tsx`, `posts/Edit.tsx`, and `Home.tsx`) received `undefined`, which renders as nothing and left the edit form's field blank so re-saving tripped the "Excerpt is required." validator. Search kept working because it filters on the `excerpt` column in SQL, before the resource ever runs. I restored the `excerpt: post.excerpt as string` line, and also restored the `toArray(): PostResourceData` return-type annotation that had been loosened to an inferred type — that annotation is what makes an omitted field a compile error rather than a silent runtime gap, so the same regression can't slip through `bun run typecheck` again. I added `tests/PostResource.test.ts` covering the serialized excerpt plus the rest of the payload; `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` is 4 pass / 0 fail.
